summary: Hassan El Mghari presents his two-year journey building AI side projects on weekends, accumulating over 8 million unique visitors, 20,000 GitHub stars, and 2.8 million signups. He stresses open source as both a passion and growth lever, attracting helpful PRs from contributors skilled in prompt engineering. Contrary to popular belief, less than 5% of his 8.5 million visitors came from his Twitter following; traffic came primarily from Google, SEO, word of mouth, and other influencers. RoomGPT, his most successful project, used the newly released control net model to redesign rooms while maintaining structural fidelity—something stable diffusion failed at. It reached 6 million visitors and 2 million registered users, with 10,000 users in the first 12 hours and 270,000 within three days. Being among the first to productionize control net drove much of this virality. Hassan demonstrates v0.dev, a Vercel product that generates UIs from prompts, streaming React components and allowing users to fork and modify designs. He shares key takeaways: use AI tools to move faster (Vercel AI SDK, v0, Replicate, Hugging Face, Modal); don't fine-tune or build custom models for MVPs—off-the-shelf APIs suffice; if you can't describe your idea in five words, it may be too complex for a weekend; use the latest models and launch early to iterate; make projects free and open source, securing sponsor credits from companies like Replicate, Bytescale, and Neon; spend ~80% of time on UI quality. He works in sprints—one intensive weekend per month (12-hour Saturday/Sunday), then relaxes. Hassan is not a trained engineer and learned coding a few years ago, emphasizing that consistent effort over many projects is the real secret.

sections.title: Introduction and Context
sections.summary: Hassan introduces his two-year journey building weekend projects. Last year: 11 projects, 20K visitors. This year: 8M+ unique visitors, 20K GitHub stars, 2.8M signups. All projects are open source at github.com/nutlope. He stresses that less than 5% of traffic comes from Twitter; most comes from word of mouth, Google, SEO, and other influencers.

sections.title: Early Projects: Alt Tags, QR-gpt, TechCrunch Summarizer
sections.summary: First AI project was an image alt-tag generator for a conference photo gallery. QR-gpt generates artistic QR codes (8K visitors). TechCrunch summarizer was taken down after legal complaints. These projects demonstrate how simple AI apps solve real problems.

sections.title: Twitter-Driven Projects: Glasses Recommender and AI Commit
sections.summary: Built glasses recommender in response to a Twitter request using LLMs and Amazon API. AI commit, a CLI tool for git commit messages, was built in under 2 hours, later packaged as npm module with 30K+ developers, 6K stars, 25 contributors.

sections.title: Twitter Bio Generator and Photo Restore
sections.summary: Twitter bio generator got 200K visitors, 100K in one weekend before hitting OpenAI bill limits. Photo restore uses gfpGAN to unblur old photos, has 250K monthly users mostly in India and Indonesia. Required TensorFlow.js moderation after inappropriate uploads. Emphasizes single API call simplicity.

sections.title: Architecture and RoomGPT Introduction
sections.summary: Describes common architecture: Next.js front/back end, upload component sends images to cloud storage, API route calls ML model, returns result to client. Introduces RoomGPT as his most successful project—give it a room and themes to generate redesigned rooms.

sections.title: RoomGPT Deep Dive and Growth
sections.summary: RoomGPT respects room structure using control net, unlike stable diffusion which distorts dimensions. Launched on Twitter, reached 10K users in 12 hours, 30K in first day, 90K in two days, 270K in three days. Being first to productionize control net drove virality. 6M total visitors, 2M registered. Most traffic from Google. Kept free and open source.

sections.title: v0.dev Demo and AI Tools
sections.summary: Demonstrates v0.dev generating an Apple Notes-style UI, forking templates, selecting elements to modify, and streaming React components via Vercel AI SDK. Recommends using AI-enhancing tools: GPT4, Vercel AI SDK, v0, Replicate, Hugging Face, Modal, and Brev to move faster.

sections.title: Key Takeaways: MVP, Models, Launch, Free, UI
sections.summary: Advises against fine-tuning or building custom models for MVPs—off-the-shelf APIs suffice. If you can't describe your idea in five words, it's too complex. Use latest models. Launch early and iterate. Make projects free and open source; secure sponsor credits from companies like Replicate, Bytescale, and Neon. Spend ~80% of time on UI since nobody uses ugly products.

sections.title: Work Style and Final Advice
sections.summary: Works in sprints—one intensive weekend per month (12-hour Saturday/Sunday), then relaxes. Emphasizes putting in hours over many projects, comparing it to gym consistency. Not a trained engineer; learned coding a few years ago. Uses Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, and Vercel. Encourages finding what works for your lifestyle.
